This page shows every active MLS® listing for detached houses in Chilliwack, BC. Here is how the local sub-areas compare.
Promontory
Promontory: hillside view homes and newer townhome complexes above Sardis, mostly built 1995–2020.
Sardis East Vedder
Sardis East Vedder: established family streets east of Vedder Road close to shops, parks and Sardis Secondary.
Garrison Crossing
Garrison Crossing: the former CFB Chilliwack base, now a walkable village of heritage-style homes, townhomes and condos.
Fairfield Island
Fairfield Island: flat, central family lots north of downtown with older ranchers and duplex-friendly zoning.
Eastern Hillsides
Eastern Hillsides: elevated view properties on Chilliwack's east slope with larger lots and acreage pockets.
Rosedale
Rosedale: small-town rural living east of Chilliwack with acreages, ranchers and farm parcels.

Detached lots are typically zoned R1-A, R1-B or R1-C (single detached), and many now allow a secondary suite or coach house under the City's small-scale multi-unit housing rules. Check the City of Chilliwack zoning map and any restrictive covenants on title before planning a suite.

Floodplain: parts of Fairfield Island, Greendale, Rosedale, Yarrow and lower Sardis lie in the Fraser and Vedder River floodplain, protected by the City's dike network. Ask for the property's flood construction level, lender and insurer requirements, and whether a geotechnical or floodplain covenant is registered on title.

Schools and transit: Chilliwack is served by School District 33 (SD33) — Sardis Secondary, G.W. Graham Middle-Secondary, Chilliwack Secondary and a range of elementary catchments including Unsworth, Watson and Vedder. Always confirm catchment with SD33 before buying. BC Transit runs Chilliwack routes along Vedder Road, Luckakuck Way and Young Road, and the Fraser Valley Express (Route 66) links Chilliwack to Abbotsford and Carvolth Exchange in Langley.

Where are detached houses for sale in Chilliwack usually located?

Most detached houses in Chilliwack come up in Promontory, Sardis East Vedder, Garrison Crossing, Fairfield Island, Eastern Hillsides and Rosedale. Each area has its own mix of age, lot size and price, so I recommend shortlisting two or three neighbourhoods before you book showings.
How often do these Chilliwack house listings update?
Listings on this page update directly from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board MLS® feed several times a day, so new listings, price changes and sold statuses appear quickly.
What should I check on zoning, strata or ALR before buying a Chilliwack house?

Detached lots are typically zoned R1-A, R1-B or R1-C (single detached), and many now allow a secondary suite or coach house under the City's small-scale multi-unit housing rules. Check the City of Chilliwack zoning map and any restrictive covenants on title before planning a suite.
Are any Chilliwack detached houses in the floodplain?

Floodplain: parts of Fairfield Island, Greendale, Rosedale, Yarrow and lower Sardis lie in the Fraser and Vedder River floodplain, protected by the City's dike network. Ask for the property's flood construction level, lender and insurer requirements, and whether a geotechnical or floodplain covenant is registered on title.
Which schools serve Chilliwack detached houses?

Chilliwack is in School District 33 (SD33). Sardis and the south side feed into Sardis Secondary and G.W. Graham, while the north side feeds Chilliwack Secondary. Catchments change, so confirm with SD33 for a specific address.
Is public transit available near Chilliwack detached houses?

Yes. BC Transit runs local Chilliwack routes along Vedder Road, Luckakuck Way and Young Road, and the Fraser Valley Express connects to Abbotsford and Langley. Rural areas such as Ryder Lake, Greendale and Columbia Valley have little or no bus service.
